title: Map independent audit coverage of #4100's obligations (navigation; no new κ)
body:
## Summary

This adds one navigation file, `docs/research/pr4100-audit-coverage-map.md`. It maps each obligation row of #4100's AUDIT.md (Cinna Davis's proposed unconditional construction) to the open audits that address it. Each entry gives the exact PR head, the outcome that PR reports, and what remains.

Current priorities say a short session can produce "an acceptance coverage map" for the #4100 audit. About 40 PRs and discussion threads now audit pieces of #4100, and none indexes them, so the next auditor can't easily see what is done.

**Claim type: consolidation / navigation. No new κ, no scientific acceptance.** No package was replayed and no proof rechecked. Outcomes are as each PR reports them. Priorities, the catalogue, the family record and the selected record are unchanged.

## What the map shows

- **Audited with a positive scoped result:** CRT §1–§4 (#4195, #4192, #4174, #4169, #4187, #4201/#4208), the free-word tensor lift (#4184), the normal form (#4215), header densities (#4227/#4228), HALO (#4217), the narrow and broad conditioning (#4282, #4193), the block solve (#4186), the Gaussian circuits (#4198/#4205/#4209/#4220), and the root/ledger (#4171).
- **Reported corrections to #4100 statements:**
  - #4178: the common-grid allocation omits the incoming height `t0`.
  - #4282: INVERSE-CONDITIONING's compression sentence does not cover circular sections; the PR repairs it.
  - #4217: a HALO constant should be `2g`, not `g`; the margin absorbs it.
  - #4237: the 49,911-child fallback bound is not sharp; 33,269 is.
  - #4228: the bad-fraction bound sharpens to `(r+1)/q`.
- **No audit found at the check:**
  - BIT.md: weighted leaves and fast header routes, and the row-stock and fixed-tape induction.
  - PROOF.md: chirp tables and the transform, CRT-composition and exact-recovery argument.
  - GAUSSIAN.md: the per-visit union schedule and the fine-prime interval at #4100's parameters.
  - GAUSSIAN.md: the all-size narrow row-gap estimate. Only `p=19` instances exist (#4304–#4309), and they depend on the chirp origin.
  - CRT: exception sorting and reinsertion, and the full `E(p,ell)` evaluator.
  - COMPLEX.md: arbitrary-f complete-cover execution.

## Task and overlap

- Card: `uniform-transfer-audit`, refined to "acceptance coverage map" (consolidation work), priority revision 7.
- Base: canonical main `12fa8c5c844be21bfefb38a19503fbd867a11244`. #4100 is pinned at `337d04939571a637aeab54a0f58f54fde811663a`.
- Overlap: `find_overlap.py` refreshed at 06:50 UTC (419 open PRs, 3,174 discussion records, complete pagination). A closed-PR search found one #4100 hit (#4165), which is not an audit. No existing #4100 coverage map or audit index was found.
- I first started an INVERSE-CONDITIONING audit at its GAUSSIAN.md caller. I dropped it after finding that #4282 (jwr404) already records the same circular-section gap.
- Refreshed again before submission. One new related PR, #4309, is included.

## Checks run

- Every relative link and anchor in the new file resolves, checked with a local script.
- `python3 -B tests/test_research_assignment.py`: 16 tests OK.
- `python3 -B tests/test_research_coordination.py`: 8 tests OK.
- `python3 -B tests/test_research_current_status.py`: 6 tests OK.

## Limitations

- The map summarizes PR bodies. It does not read package contents.
- "None found" means no matching open record existed at the check time. It does not prove novelty.
- Heads will move. Each row should be rechecked before use.
- I did not link the map from `research-family-status.md` or `current-priorities.md`, since those belong to the director's priority review. A maintainer can add a link from the #4100 row if the map is useful.

## Credit

All mathematical results belong to the cited authors: Cinna Davis (#4100), kumagi/Hiroki KUMAZAKI, ToikY, jmbarrancoml, petalas, yssite and jwr404. Prepared by Ryanson Jonathan with substantial Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) assistance. Apache-2.0.

## Workflow feedback (optional)

The overlap helper made a complete snapshot easy. Finding every audit of one large proposal still meant reading about 40 bodies, because many cite AUDIT.md premises in prose rather than as a structured field. An optional `audits: {pr, file, premise}` entry in TASK.json would make maps like this one mechanical.
